events.title: Early Cycladic culture emerges
events.description: Island communities across the Cyclades begin producing the marble figurines and fine pottery that mark the start of Aegean civilisation.

events.title: First Minoan palaces at Knossos
events.description: Complex palace societies appear on Crete, with storerooms, workshops and administration on a scale not seen before in the Aegean.

events.title: Linear A writing appears
events.description: Minoan scribes begin using a syllabic script for palace accounting. It has never been deciphered.

events.title: Minoan palaces rebuilt after destruction
events.description: Earthquakes level the first palaces; grander complexes rise on the ruins at Knossos, Phaistos and Malia.

events.title: Thera erupts
events.description: One of the largest volcanic eruptions in human history buries Akrotiri and sends ash and tsunami across the Aegean, damaging Minoan Crete.

events.title: Mycenaeans take control of Crete
events.description: Mainland Greeks occupy the Minoan palaces. Linear B, an early form of Greek, replaces Linear A in the records.

events.title: Mycenae reaches its height
events.description: The citadel above the Argolid plain dominates a network of palace states, its shaft graves filled with gold.

events.title: Lion Gate built at Mycenae
events.description: The monumental gateway and the great cyclopean walls go up, the most recognisable surviving image of Mycenaean power.

events.title: Traditional date of the Trojan War
events.description: Later Greeks placed Agamemnon's expedition against Troy in this period. Whether it happened is still argued.

events.title: Mycenaean palaces burn
events.description: Pylos, Mycenae and Tiryns are destroyed within a generation as the wider Bronze Age world collapses.

events.title: Linear B falls out of use
events.description: Writing disappears from Greece for roughly four centuries as the palace bureaucracies that needed it vanish.

events.title: Ionian migration to Asia Minor
events.description: Greeks cross the Aegean and settle the coast of Anatolia, founding Miletus, Ephesus and their neighbours.

events.title: Iron working spreads
events.description: Iron replaces bronze for tools and weapons across the Greek world during the recovery from the collapse.

events.title: Greek alphabet adopted
events.description: Greeks adapt the Phoenician alphabet and add vowels, producing the first writing system to record speech fully.

events.title: First Olympic Games
events.description: The games at Olympia become the fixed point from which later Greeks counted their history.

events.title: Homeric epics take written form
events.description: The Iliad and Odyssey are set down after generations of oral performance, becoming the shared inheritance of Greek culture.

events.title: Colonisation of Sicily and Italy begins
events.description: Land hunger and trade push Greeks west; Syracuse, Naxos and dozens of other cities are founded.

events.title: Age of the tyrants
events.description: Populist strongmen seize power in Corinth, Sicyon and elsewhere, breaking the grip of the old aristocracies.

events.title: Draco's law code at Athens
events.description: Athens receives its first written laws. Their severity gave English the word draconian.

events.title: Solon's reforms
events.description: Solon cancels debts, bans debt slavery and opens the assembly, laying the groundwork for Athenian democracy.

events.title: Persia absorbs the Ionian cities
events.description: Cyrus the Great's conquest of Lydia brings the Greek cities of Asia Minor under Persian rule.

events.title: Cleisthenes founds Athenian democracy
events.description: The reforms reorganise Athens by deme rather than clan and hand real power to the assembly of citizens.

events.title: Ionian Revolt
events.description: The Greek cities of Asia Minor rise against Persia with Athenian help. Its failure brings Persian retaliation.

events.title: Battle of Marathon
events.description: An outnumbered Athenian force defeats the first Persian invasion on the plain north-east of the city.

events.title: Thermopylae and Salamis
events.description: Leonidas dies holding the pass; weeks later the Athenian fleet destroys the Persian navy in the straits off Salamis.

events.title: Battle of Plataea ends the invasion
events.description: A combined Greek army defeats the Persian land force, ending the attempt to conquer the mainland.

events.title: Delian League formed
events.description: Athens leads an alliance against Persia. Its treasury on Delos soon funds an Athenian empire in all but name.

events.title: Ephialtes strips the Areopagus
events.description: The old aristocratic council loses its powers to the assembly and courts, completing the democratic settlement.

events.title: Pericles rises to leadership
events.description: For three decades Pericles guides Athens through its cultural peak and into ruinous war.

events.title: Parthenon begun
events.description: Work starts on the temple of Athena on the Acropolis, funded from the league treasury moved to Athens.

events.title: Sophocles stages Antigone
events.description: Athenian tragedy reaches its height in the work of Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides.

events.title: Peloponnesian War begins
events.description: Sparta and its allies go to war with the Athenian empire. The struggle lasts twenty-seven years.

events.title: Plague strikes Athens
events.description: An epidemic kills perhaps a third of the population crowded inside the walls, Pericles among them.

events.title: Sicilian Expedition sails
events.description: Athens gambles on conquering Syracuse. The entire force is destroyed within two years.

events.title: Athens surrenders
events.description: The long walls come down and Sparta installs the Thirty Tyrants. Athenian empire is finished.

events.title: Socrates executed
events.description: Condemned for impiety and corrupting the young, he drinks hemlock rather than flee.

events.title: Plato founds the Academy
events.description: The school outside the walls of Athens shapes Western philosophy for nine centuries.

events.title: Thebes breaks Spartan power
events.description: Epaminondas defeats Sparta at Leuctra, ending its dominance of the Greek mainland.

events.title: Philip II wins at Chaeronea
events.description: Macedon defeats a Greek coalition and imposes unity on the city states.

events.title: Aristotle founds the Lyceum
events.description: Having tutored Alexander, Aristotle returns to Athens to teach and to catalogue nearly everything then known.

events.title: Alexander invades Persia
events.description: At twenty-two he crosses the Hellespont with a Macedonian and Greek army and never returns.

events.title: Battle of Gaugamela
events.description: Darius III is defeated decisively and the Persian Empire passes to Alexander.

events.title: Alexandria founded
events.description: The new city on the Egyptian coast becomes the intellectual capital of the Greek world.

events.title: Alexander reaches the Indus
events.description: His army refuses to go further east and the campaign turns back.

events.title: Alexander dies at Babylon
events.description: Aged thirty-two, leaving no viable heir. His generals divide the empire between them.

events.title: The Successor kingdoms form
events.description: Ptolemy in Egypt, Seleucus in Asia and Antigonus in Macedon take royal titles, splitting Alexander's conquests.

events.title: Euclid writes the Elements
events.description: At Alexandria he sets out the geometry that will be taught for over two thousand years.

events.title: Library of Alexandria founded
events.description: The Ptolemies gather Greek learning into the ancient world's greatest research institution.

events.title: Archimedes at work in Syracuse
events.description: His work on levers, buoyancy and the measurement of curves is unmatched until the seventeenth century.

events.title: Eratosthenes measures the Earth
events.description: Using shadows at Alexandria and Syene he calculates the circumference to within a few per cent.

events.title: Rome defeats Macedon at Cynoscephalae
events.description: Roman legions beat the Macedonian phalanx, and Rome declares the Greek cities free.

events.title: Battle of Pydna ends the Macedonian kingdom
events.description: Macedon is broken into republics and then annexed outright.

events.title: Rome sacks Corinth
events.description: The Achaean League is crushed and Greece is absorbed into the Roman world.

events.title: Sulla storms Athens
events.description: Athens backs Mithridates against Rome and is stormed and looted for it.

events.title: Battle of Actium
events.description: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra off the Greek coast, ending the Hellenistic age for good.

events.title: Achaea becomes a Roman province
events.description: Augustus reorganises Greece as a senatorial province governed from Corinth.

events.title: Paul preaches at Athens and Corinth
events.description: Christian communities are planted in the Greek cities, among the earliest anywhere.

events.title: Hadrian rebuilds Athens
events.description: The philhellene emperor completes the Temple of Olympian Zeus and endows the city lavishly.

events.title: Herulian sack of Athens
events.description: Germanic raiders break into Greece and burn the centre of Athens.

events.title: Greece under the Tetrarchy
events.description: Diocletian's reorganisation divides the provinces and shifts imperial attention east.

events.title: Constantinople founded
events.description: Constantine refounds Byzantium as the new capital. The Greek east becomes the centre of the Roman world.

events.title: Olympic Games abolished
events.description: Theodosius bans pagan festivals; the games at Olympia end after more than a thousand years.

events.title: Justinian closes the Academy
events.description: The Athenian philosophical schools are shut, marking a symbolic end to classical antiquity.

events.title: Slavic settlement in Greece
events.description: Slavic groups move into the Balkan interior and much of the Greek countryside for two centuries.

events.title: Iconoclast controversy begins
events.description: The dispute over religious images convulses the empire and its Greek provinces for over a century.

events.title: Byzantine reconquest of the Peloponnese
events.description: Imperial authority is restored across southern Greece and the region is resettled.

events.title: Great Lavra founded on Mount Athos
events.description: The monastic republic on the Athos peninsula becomes the spiritual centre of Orthodox Greece.

events.title: Basil II completes the Bulgarian conquest
events.description: The northern frontier is secured and Greece enjoys a long period of stability and growth.

events.title: East-West Schism
events.description: Rome and Constantinople excommunicate one another, dividing Latin and Orthodox Christendom.

events.title: Defeat at Manzikert
events.description: The loss to the Seljuk Turks opens Anatolia and begins the long Byzantine decline.

events.title: Venice granted trading privileges
events.description: Byzantine concessions hand Venetian merchants the commerce of the Aegean.

events.title: Normans sack Thessaloniki
events.description: The empire's second city is taken and plundered by a Sicilian Norman force.

events.title: Fourth Crusade takes Constantinople
events.description: Crusaders sack the capital and carve the empire into Latin states. Greece is parcelled out to western lords.

events.title: Frankish principalities established
events.description: The Principality of Achaea and the Duchy of Athens are set up under French rulers.

events.title: Venice takes Crete
events.description: The island becomes a Venetian colony for more than four centuries.

events.title: Byzantine victory at Pelagonia
events.description: Nicaean forces defeat the Frankish coalition and open the way to recovering the capital.

events.title: Constantinople recovered
events.description: Michael VIII restores the Byzantine Empire, though it never regains its former strength.

events.title: Black Death reaches Greece
events.description: Plague arrives through the trading ports and kills a large part of the population.

events.title: Despotate of the Morea founded
events.description: A Byzantine principality centred on Mystras rules the Peloponnese and enjoys a late cultural flowering.

events.title: Ottomans take Thessaloniki for the first time
events.description: The great northern city changes hands repeatedly as Ottoman power advances.

events.title: Constantine XI crowned at Mystras
events.description: The last Byzantine emperor is crowned in the Peloponnese before travelling to the doomed capital.

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.description: Mehmed II takes the city. The Byzantine Empire ends and Greek scholars flee west, feeding the Renaissance.

events.title: Ottomans conquer the Morea
events.description: The Despotate falls and the Peloponnese passes under Ottoman rule.

events.title: The millet system
events.description: Orthodox Greeks are governed through their church, which preserves language and faith under Ottoman rule.

events.title: Battle of Lepanto
events.description: A Christian fleet destroys the Ottoman navy off the western Greek coast, with many Greek crews aboard.

events.title: Klephts take to the mountains
events.description: Bandit-fighters in the highlands become the folk heroes and later the manpower of the independence struggle.

events.title: Venice loses Crete
events.description: Candia falls after a twenty-one year siege, the longest in recorded history.

events.title: Parthenon explodes
events.description: A Venetian shell hits the Ottoman powder magazine inside the temple, wrecking the building.

events.title: Orlov Revolt
events.description: A Russian-backed rising in the Peloponnese fails and is put down harshly.

events.title: Treaty of Kucuk Kaynarca
events.description: Russia gains the right to protect Ottoman Orthodox Christians, and Greek merchant shipping expands rapidly.

events.title: Filiki Eteria founded
events.description: A secret society formed among Greek merchants in Odessa begins organising for revolution.

events.title: Greek War of Independence begins
events.description: Revolt breaks out in the Peloponnese and spreads. It will take nine years and foreign intervention to win.

events.title: Chios massacre
events.description: Ottoman forces kill or enslave most of the island's population. The atrocity turns European opinion.

events.title: Byron dies at Missolonghi
events.description: The poet's death fighting for Greece makes the cause famous across Europe.

events.title: Battle of Navarino
events.description: British, French and Russian fleets destroy the Ottoman-Egyptian navy, making independence certain.

events.title: London Protocol recognises Greece
events.description: The powers acknowledge an independent Greek state, though a small one.

events.title: Otto of Bavaria becomes king
events.description: The powers install a seventeen-year-old Bavarian prince as the first king of Greece.

events.title: Athens becomes the capital
events.description: The government moves from Nafplio to a town of a few thousand people beneath the Acropolis.

events.title: Britain cedes the Ionian Islands
events.description: Corfu and its neighbours are handed to Greece, and a new constitution makes the country a crowned democracy.

events.title: Corinth Canal opens
events.description: The cut through the isthmus, first attempted by Nero, is finally completed.

events.title: First modern Olympics in Athens
events.description: The games are revived in the Panathenaic Stadium, fourteen centuries after they were banned.

events.title: Balkan Wars begin
events.description: Greece nearly doubles in size, gaining Thessaloniki, Epirus, Crete and the northern Aegean islands.

events.title: Greek landing at Smyrna
events.description: Encouraged by the Allies, Greece occupies the Anatolian coast in pursuit of the Great Idea.

events.title: Asia Minor Catastrophe
events.description: The Greek army collapses, Smyrna burns, and the Anatolian Greek presence of three thousand years ends.

events.title: Population exchange with Turkey
events.description: Some 1.2 million Orthodox Christians move to Greece and 400,000 Muslims the other way.

events.title: Second Hellenic Republic declared
events.description: The monarchy is abolished by referendum after the Anatolian disaster, beginning decades of instability.

events.title: Metaxas dictatorship
events.description: General Metaxas suspends parliament and rules until his death, on a corporatist model.

events.title: Greece refuses Mussolini's ultimatum
events.description: The Italian invasion is thrown back into Albania, the first Allied land victory of the war.

events.title: German invasion and occupation
events.description: Germany intervenes, Greece falls, and a famine follows that kills perhaps 300,000 people in Athens alone.

events.title: Destruction of Greek Jewry
events.description: Over 45,000 Jews are deported from Thessaloniki to Auschwitz; the community is almost entirely destroyed.

events.title: Liberation and the Dekemvriana
events.description: German withdrawal is followed within weeks by fighting in Athens between the resistance and government forces.

events.title: Civil War begins
events.description: Communist and government forces fight for three years, leaving the country devastated and dependent on Western aid.

events.title: Greece joins NATO
events.description: Cold War alignment is settled, and women vote in national elections for the first time.

events.title: Colonels seize power
events.description: A military junta rules for seven years, imprisoning and exiling opponents.

events.title: Athens Polytechnic uprising
events.description: Tanks crush a student occupation. The date becomes the symbol of resistance to the junta.

events.title: Junta falls and the republic returns
events.description: The Cyprus crisis brings down the colonels; a referendum abolishes the monarchy for good.

events.title: Greece joins the European Community
events.description: Membership anchors the new democracy in western Europe and brings substantial development funds.

events.title: Greece adopts the euro
events.description: The drachma, in use in some form since antiquity, is replaced by the single currency.

events.title: Athens hosts the Olympics
events.description: The games return to their birthplace, and Greece wins the European football championship the same summer.

events.title: Debt crisis and bailout
events.description: Greece loses market access and accepts the first of three rescue programs, with austerity that shrinks the economy by a quarter.

events.title: Bailout referendum and capital controls
events.description: Voters reject the creditors' terms; the government accepts a third program regardless.

events.title: Greece exits the bailout programs
events.description: After eight years the country returns to market funding, with debt still among the highest in Europe.
